_about: Date-versioned IRDAI / Ombudsman rules used by the engine. 'status': in_force = primary text or several consistent sources checked; reported = secondary sources only; draft = only the draft text was verified. Check the IRDAI website before relying on any rule in a dispute.

rules.title: Room-rent cut applies only to 'associate medical expenses'
rules.plain: If you stay in a room above your limit, the insurer may cut related charges in the same proportion, but not pharmacy (medicines), implants and medical devices, or diagnostics (tests).
rules.date_note: Draft circular dated 17 Mar 2020 (verified). Business Standard (12 Jun 2020) reported the final guidelines with the same exclusions.

source.name: IRDAI guidelines on product filing in health insurance: norms for proportionate deductions

rules.title: No room-rent proportionate cut on ICU charges
rules.plain: Insurers are not allowed to apply the proportionate cut to ICU charges, because there are no ICU categories to compare against.
rules.date_note: Same circular as PROP-01.

source.name: IRDAI guidelines on product filing in health insurance: norms for proportionate deductions

rules.title: No proportionate cut where the hospital does not bill by room category
rules.plain: If the hospital charges the same for doctors, nursing and OT whatever room you pick (no 'differential billing'), the insurer must not apply the proportionate cut.
rules.date_note: Same circular as PROP-01.

source.name: IRDAI guidelines on product filing in health insurance: norms for proportionate deductions

rules.title: IRDAI standard lists of optional and subsumed items (Lists I to IV)
rules.plain: List I items (68, e.g. gloves, masks, diapers, certificates) are optional: the insurer may choose not to pay them. List II (37), III (23) and IV (18) items must be included in room, procedure or treatment charges, so the hospital should not bill them separately.
rules.date_note: Applies to products filed on or after 1 Oct 2019; non-compliant older products could not be offered after 1 Oct 2020.

source.name: IRDAI: Modification of Guidelines on Standardization in Health Insurance

rules.title: Moratorium after 8 years (96 months) of continuous cover
rules.plain: After 96 continuous months of cover, the insurer could not contest a claim for non-disclosure or misrepresentation, except for proven fraud.
rules.date_note: Replaced by the 60-month moratorium from 1 Apr 2024.

source.name: IRDAI guidelines on standardization (moratorium period)

rules.title: Moratorium after 5 years (60 months) of continuous cover
rules.plain: After 60 continuous months of cover (portability and migration count), no policy or claim can be contested for non-disclosure or misrepresentation, except for established fraud. If the sum insured was increased, the 60 months count from the increase, for the extra amount only.
rules.date_note: IRDAI health insurance reforms effective 1 Apr 2024, consolidated in the Master Circular on Health Insurance Business (29 May 2024).

source.name: IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business

rules.title: Pre-existing disease waiting period: at most 48 months
rules.plain: Before 1 Apr 2024, the waiting period for pre-existing diseases could be up to 4 years.
rules.date_note: Replaced by the 36-month cap from 1 Apr 2024.

source.name: Business Today: IRDAI reduces PED waiting period from 4 to 3 years

rules.title: Pre-existing disease waiting period: at most 36 months
rules.plain: From 1 Apr 2024, the waiting period for pre-existing diseases can be at most 3 years. Insurers may set a shorter period.
rules.date_note: Effective 1 Apr 2024.

source.name: Business Today: IRDAI reduces PED waiting period from 4 to 3 years

rules.title: Cashless: decide in 1 hour, approve discharge in 3 hours
rules.plain: Insurers must decide a cashless request within 1 hour and give final discharge approval within 3 hours of the hospital's request. If discharge approval is late, any extra hospital charges are paid by the insurer from its shareholders' fund.
rules.date_note: Timelines applied from 1 Aug 2024 (Lok Sabha data and several reports).

source.name: IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business

rules.title: No rejection for want of documents; insurer collects documents
rules.plain: Policyholders should not have to chase documents: insurers and TPAs should collect them from the hospital. No claim shall be rejected or closed for want of documents or for delayed intimation.
rules.date_note: Stated in a Rajya Sabha answer (11 Feb 2025) and reported on the Master Circular's release.

source.name: IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business, as stated in a Rajya Sabha answer
source.reference: Rajya Sabha PQ, 11 Feb 2025; Master Circular 29 May 2024

rules.title: Rejections need Claims Review Committee approval and must cite the policy clause
rules.plain: A claim can be rejected only with the approval of the insurer's three-member Claims Review Committee, and the rejection must state the specific policy terms it relies on.
rules.date_note: From the Master Circular on Health Insurance Business (29 May 2024), as reported.

source.name: IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business

rules.title: Genuine claims must not be rejected only for late intimation
rules.plain: IRDAI told insurers not to reject genuine claims only because they were intimated or submitted late, where the delay had a good reason. Late claims must be decided on merit.
rules.date_note: Sources date the circular 20 or 29 Sep 2011. Courts (e.g. NCDRC 2018) apply it.

source.name: IRDA circular on rejection of claims on the ground of delay

rules.title: Settle or reject within 30 days of the last document; interest if late
rules.plain: The insurer must settle or reject a claim within 30 days of receiving the last necessary document (45 days if it investigates). If it pays late, it owes interest at 2% above the bank rate.
rules.date_note: IRDAI (Protection of Policyholders' Interests) Regulations, 2017, as reported.

source.name: IRDAI (Protection of Policyholders' Interests) Regulations, 2017

rules.title: Insurer must resolve a grievance within 14 days
rules.plain: Insurers must acknowledge a complaint immediately and resolve it within 14 days, giving reasons tied to the policy terms if they do not accept it.
rules.date_note: Text verified from the Master Circular (5 Sep 2024). The 14-day limit is in Part A, complaints mechanism.

source.name: IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024
source.reference: IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024 dated 5 Sep 2024, turnaround time for resolution of complaints

rules.title: When you can go to the Insurance Ombudsman
rules.plain: First complain to the insurer in writing. You can go to the Ombudsman if the insurer rejects it, does not reply within one month, or you are not satisfied with the reply. File within one year of the insurer's reply (or within one year after the one-month period if there was no reply). The same matter must not be pending in a court or consumer forum. The service is free.
rules.date_note: Rule 14(3) and 14(5), Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (as amended). Text verified from the Council for Insurance Ombudsmen.

source.name: Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (as amended)

rules.title: Ombudsman award limit: Rs 30 lakh
rules.plain: The Ombudsman could award at most Rs 30 lakh (including expenses).
rules.date_note: Rule 17(3) of the 2017 Rules as amended in 2021 (text verified).

source.name: Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (as amended 2021)

rules.title: Ombudsman award limit: Rs 50 lakh
rules.plain: The Ombudsman can award up to Rs 50 lakh (including expenses), never more than your actual loss.
rules.date_note: Amendment notified as G.S.R. 828(E) dated 9 Nov 2023 (reported).

source.name: Insurance Ombudsman (Amendment) Rules, 2023

rules.title: With several health policies, you choose which to claim first
rules.plain: If you hold more than one indemnity health policy, you can choose the policy to claim under, and claim the balance or the disallowed amount under another policy. You cannot recover the same expense twice.
rules.date_note: IRDAI 2017 clarification and standard policy wording, as reported.

source.name: IRDAI rules on multiple health policies
source.reference: 2017 clarification; Master Circular on Health Insurance Business

rules.title: Health policy grace period: 30 days (15 days for monthly premiums)
rules.plain: If you miss the renewal or premium date, you get a grace period of 30 days (15 days if you pay monthly). Renewing within it keeps all your credits: sum insured, no-claim bonus, waiting periods already served and moratorium months. Cover during the grace period is guaranteed only when the premium is paid in instalments.
rules.date_note: Text verified from the Master Circular (29 May 2024).

source.name: IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business
source.reference: IRDAI/HLT/CIR/PRO/84/5/2024 dated 29 May 2024, Chapter I paras 8 and 9

rules.title: Renewal cannot be refused because you claimed
rules.plain: A health policy must be renewed (unless the product is withdrawn, or there was established fraud, non-disclosure or misrepresentation). The insurer cannot deny renewal because you made claims, and cannot underwrite you again unless you ask for a higher sum insured.
rules.date_note: Text verified from the Master Circular (29 May 2024).

source.name: IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business
source.reference: IRDAI/HLT/CIR/PRO/84/5/2024 dated 29 May 2024, Chapter I para 10

rules.title: Porting or migrating keeps your waiting-period credits
rules.plain: When you move to another insurer (portability) or another policy of the same insurer (migration), the credits you earned move with you: sum insured, no-claim bonus, specific and pre-existing disease waiting periods served, and moratorium months. Buying a fresh policy instead starts them again.
rules.date_note: Text verified from the Master Circular (29 May 2024).

source.name: IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business
source.reference: IRDAI/HLT/CIR/PRO/84/5/2024 dated 29 May 2024, Chapter I paras 11 to 13

rules.title: Senior citizens: premium rises above 10% a year need IRDAI consultation
rules.plain: For individual indemnity health policies of people aged 60 and above, insurers must not raise the premium by more than 10% a year without first consulting IRDAI.
rules.date_note: IRDAI circular IRDAI/HLT/CIR/MISC/27/1/2025 dated 30 Jan 2025, as reported by several outlets.

source.name: IRDAI circular on premium revision for senior citizens

rules.title: Life policy grace period: 30 days (15 days for monthly premiums)
rules.plain: A life policy has a grace period of 30 days after the premium due date (15 days for monthly premiums). During it the policy stays in force and the life cover continues. If the premium is not paid by then, the policy lapses; it can usually be revived within the period the policy allows.
rules.date_note: Text verified from the Master Circular (5 Sep 2024).

source.name: IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024
source.reference: IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024 dated 5 Sep 2024, Part A: grace period, lapse and revival

rules.title: After 3 years a life policy cannot be questioned on any ground
rules.plain: No life insurance policy can be called in question on any ground after 3 years from the policy date: the later of the issue date, the start of risk, the revival date or the rider date (Section 45, Insurance Act, 1938). Within those 3 years the insurer can question it only for fraud or for a wrong or hidden material fact, and must give its reasons in writing.
rules.date_note: Section 45 as amended by the Insurance Laws (Amendment) Act, 2015. The 3-year rule is restated in the IRDAI Master Circular of 5 Sep 2024 (text verified); the grounds within 3 years are in Section 45(2) and 45(4).

source.name: IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024
source.reference: Section 45, Insurance Act, 1938; IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024 dated 5 Sep 2024, Part A: policy cannot be contested

rules.title: No claim rejected for missing documents or late intimation; rejection needs evidence
rules.plain: No claim shall be rejected or closed because documents are missing or because it was intimated late. No claim shall be repudiated without legally tenable evidence.
rules.date_note: Text verified from the Master Circular (5 Sep 2024).

source.name: IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024
source.reference: IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024 dated 5 Sep 2024, Part A: at the time of claim

rules.title: Death claims: settle in 15 days (45 if investigated), or pay interest
rules.plain: A life insurer must settle a death claim within 15 days of the claim being intimated, or within 45 days if the claim needs investigation. If it is late, it must pay interest at the bank rate plus 2% from the date of intimation until payment, on its own, along with the claim.
rules.date_note: Text verified from the Master Circular (5 Sep 2024).

source.name: IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024
source.reference: IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024 dated 5 Sep 2024, Part A: turnaround time for settlement of claims

rules.title: Nomination is mandatory for life policies and can be changed any time
rules.plain: A nominee is needed so the claim can be paid on the death of the life assured. You can name more than one nominee with a share for each, appoint someone to receive the money for a minor nominee, and change the nomination at any time during the policy.
rules.date_note: Text verified from the Master Circular (5 Sep 2024).

source.name: IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024
source.reference: IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024 dated 5 Sep 2024, Part A: nomination

rules.title: Only a spouse, parent or child can be a 'beneficial nominee'
rules.plain: Under Section 39 of the Insurance Act (amended 2015), a nominee who is the policyholder's spouse, parent or child can be a beneficial nominee. Any other nominee receives the money on behalf of the legal heirs. Courts differ on how far even a beneficial nominee excludes legal heirs, so a Will is the surest way to decide who keeps the money.
rules.date_note: Section 39(7), Insurance Act, 1938 as amended in 2015; High Court rulings differ on its effect (2023-2025).

source.name: Trilegal / Mondaq: the rights of nominees of insurance policies explained

rules.title: A lender gets only the outstanding loan from a death claim
rules.plain: If a life policy is assigned to a bank or lender for a loan, the lender is paid only the outstanding loan on the date of death. The balance of the death benefit is paid directly to the nominee's bank account.
rules.date_note: Text verified from the Master Circular (5 Sep 2024).

source.name: IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024
source.reference: IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024 dated 5 Sep 2024, Part A: at the time of claim (assigned policies)

rules.title: Search for unclaimed insurance money on Bima Bharosa
rules.plain: Money owed by an insurer and unpaid for over 12 months is an 'unclaimed amount'. Search for it on Bima Bharosa (bimabharosa.irdai.gov.in/Home/UnclaimedAmount) or the insurer's website using any two of: policy number, PAN, name and date of birth of the policyholder. After 10 years it moves to the Senior Citizens' Welfare Fund, and can still be claimed through the insurer for 25 more years.
rules.date_note: Text verified from the Master Circular (5 Sep 2024).

source.name: IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024
source.reference: IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024 dated 5 Sep 2024, Part A: unclaimed amount

rules.title: IRDAI does not sell policies, announce bonuses or refund money
rules.plain: IRDAI and its officials do not sell insurance, announce bonuses, invest premiums or refund amounts. Anyone calling or messaging as IRDAI about such things is a fraud: IRDAI asks people who get such calls to file a police complaint.
rules.date_note: Text verified from the Master Circular (5 Sep 2024); IRDAI has issued similar public notices since 2014.

source.name: IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024
source.reference: IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024 dated 5 Sep 2024, Part A: caution against spurious/fraudulent calls

rules.title: Pay premiums only into the insurer's own account
rules.plain: Premium must be paid only to the insurer's account, directly or through its authorised distribution channel, and you should get a valid receipt at once.
rules.date_note: Text verified from the Master Circular (5 Sep 2024).

source.name: IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024
source.reference: IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024 dated 5 Sep 2024, Part A: payment of premium

rules.title: Suicide in the first 12 months: at least 80% of premiums paid
rules.plain: Life policies usually exclude death by suicide within 12 months of the start or revival of the policy. Even then, the nominee is entitled to at least 80% of the premiums paid (or the fund value for a unit-linked policy). After 12 months, the policy's normal death benefit applies.
rules.date_note: IRDAI product regulations (non-linked and linked products), as reported by insurers and consumer sites.

source.name: IRDAI product regulations on the suicide clause (as reported)
source.reference: IRDAI (Non-Linked / Unit Linked Insurance Products) Regulations
